layers.label: FOUNDATIONS
layers.interpretation: Builds the mathematical, statistical, computational and programming base used later in the programme.

curriculumMeaning.why: Problem solving, algorithms and software foundations
Modelling, linear algebra, calculus and optimisation foundations
Probability, uncertainty, inference and data interpretation

layers.label: PROGRAMMING + DATA SYSTEMS
layers.interpretation: Moves from programming foundations into databases, data structures, application development and systems tooling.

courses.name: Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms using Python

layers.label: DATA SCIENCE CORE
layers.interpretation: Develops data management, machine-learning foundations, model practice and practical data-science tooling.

courses.name: Introduction to Deep Learning and Generative AI
Deep Learning and Generative AI - Project

layers.optionNote: The official curriculum page states that Diploma in Data Science learners choose one of these two 6-credit option tracks.

layers.label: DEGREE-LEVEL COMPUTING + AI
layers.interpretation: Adds software-engineering discipline and degree-level AI/deep-learning core work; electives vary by term.

coreCourses.name: AI: Search Methods for Problem Solving

layers.electivePolicy: The official programme page states that the elective list may change each term depending on availability; the portfolio therefore does not present the current elective catalogue as guaranteed future coursework.

academicConnections.note: Both public projects already use Python/software systems. The curriculum provides a formal programming and algorithms pathway; this is a conceptual connection, not a claim that IITM coursework caused the projects.
Halim Nexus AI uses SQLite persistence. Database Management Systems is an official later curriculum component.
Statistical reasoning and data interpretation are relevant to research-method decisions; this does not claim completed statistics coursework.

The project and research record already engage AI-related questions. Machine-learning and AI courses appear later in the official curriculum; the relationship is conceptual until coursework is verified.
Existing projects provide system-building evidence; Software Engineering and Software Testing appear at degree level.
